title: Tensoring bounded-above acyclic complexes with bounded-above flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $A^\bullet$ be a bounded-above acyclic cochain complex of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded-above cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then the total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}P^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is acyclic.

source.place: Lemma 06YS, bounded-above case in the proof (the first-quadrant spectral sequence with $E_1^{p,q}=H^p(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}P^q)$)

proof.text: Reduce acyclicity to exactness at each integer degree using the fixed-degree truncation theorem [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-tensor-acyclic-degree].

source.place: Lemma 06YQ, bounded-above case; truncation to a bounded double complex so that Homology Lemma 0132 applies

proof.text: Use the second spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] for E, filtered by the P'-degree q. Its E_1-term in position q is H^p_I(E^{\bullet,q})=H^p(B^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}P'^q), the first differential being that of B. For each q, P'^q is either 0 or the flat module P^q, so the functor -\otimes_{\mathcal O}P'^q is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and carries the exact sequences B^{p-1}\to B^p\to B^{p+1} to exact sequences; by the definition of acyclicity [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], B^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}P'^q is acyclic. Hence every E_1-term vanishes.

source.place: Lemma 06YQ, bounded-above case: E_1^{p,q}=H^p(L^\bullet\otimes K^q) and flatness of K^q

proof.text: All later pages are subquotients of the E_1-page, so E_\infty=0. By [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] the image filtration on H^n(\operatorname{Tot}E) is finite (F^0H^n=H^n, F^{n'+1}H^n=0 after the translation) with graded pieces E_\infty=0; a finite filtration with zero graded pieces is zero, so H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)=H^n(\operatorname{Tot}E)=0. As n was arbitrary, Tot(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}P^\bullet) is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules].
